hook.line: There are only 288 completed 4×4 sudoku grids. Small enough that speed decides the game.
hook.say: Welcome to the world of Speed Sudoku!

ch.t: A big world in a small grid
ch.say: Small, but part of a mathematical family.
p: A 4×4 grid is the most familiar member of the Latin-square family behind sudoku.
Solved with just 1–4, it is loved in maths classrooms and as a speed puzzle.
st: Latin squares — 4×4 is the smallest practical one
Sudoku is named; puzzles of many sizes follow
World championships score puzzles against the clock

ch.say: Then came the age of speed.
tl: The world boom spreads small-size puzzles too
The World Sudoku Championship begins — racing the clock

ch.say: 1 to 4 once in every row, column and 2×2 box!
p: The same rules as 9×9, squeezed into 4×4.
You can see the whole grid at a glance — so it becomes a test of insight and reflexes.

items: Four clues can force a unique answer

ch.say: Tap a card to flip it!
cards: Euler used Latin letters as the symbols
Fix the first row — then how many?
Only 12 ways to finish the grid
Counting rotations and relabelling as the same, just 2, it is said
Look for the one missing digit
Is speed solving good for the brain?
It’s often used as focus training

p: Four digits to test your flashes of insight.
